evidence: Requirement-by-requirement reachability (frozen task): (1) Runtime: instruction.md:13 asks for Node.js+Express+SQLite, node /app/server.js, port 3000/PORT, GET /api/health without DB, /app/app.db honouring DB_PATH, and says server dependencies are already available so do not install packages. environment/Dockerfile:1-12 provides node:22-bookworm-slim with express@5.1.0 and better-sqlite3@12.4.1 on NODE_PATH=/usr/local/lib/node_modules plus sqlite3 CLI; integration.md:3-6 says the same. Sessions, password checks (crypto) and live updates (polling/SSE, rules.md:123) are buildable with Express + Node built-ins. tests/Dockerfile:16-22 pins the same express/better-sqlite3 versions and tests/test.sh:104-111 launches with exactly PATH, HOME, NODE_PATH, PORT=3000, DB_PATH as uid 65534, possibly from a copy (/tmp/submission), which rules.md:198-202 discloses (resolve files relative to module dir, honour DB_PATH, writable copy, unprivileged). 'start with no shipped database' (instruction.md:15) is stated, which matters because test.sh:92 copies /app as-is. The symlink restriction (test.sh:72-83) is disclosed in integration.md:16-19. (2) Network: task.toml:22,38 network_mode='public' in both phases; instruction.md:13 lets the browser use CDN fonts/scripts while the server must not depend on an outside data service. Nothing requires network, so even a no-network reading leaves every requirement reachable. (3) Seed: all accounts in instruction.md:17 exist in seed users (10: 3 recruiter, 3 hiring_manager, 1 observer, 3 candidate); one shared password stated. Seed has stages, candidate_status_labels matching rules.md:183-190, thread_page_size=30 (rules.md:144,209), 3 jobs with interview_limit 3/2/3, 16 applications with stage+position (+rejected_from/reject_reason for APP-301), 127 messages (APP-101=120), each conversation chronologically sorted with unique timestamps so 'read_count counted from its first' (rules.md:207-208) has one reading; 3 notes; 6 read markers. Candidate linkage by email (rules.md:35-36) resolves APP-101/APP-302 to Noor, APP-201 to Tomas, APP-301 to Lena. Graded seed facts re-derived: Lena APP-301 has 3 messages, read_count 2, message 3 sent by USR-REC3 -> 1 unread (functional Z / hro_unread_counts); PLAT Applied order Greta, Ade, Marco and Screen Priya, Samuel by position; Noor APP-101 note text matches (hro_restart). Paging 120 -> 30 shown with 90/60/30/0 remaining is derivable. (4) Single-reading check of the rules against what is graded: one-stage moves and skip refusal (rules.md:47-48); reject needs reason and remembers stage; reopen only to that stage (49-51); bottom arrival (57-58); interview places incl. bulk and undo (63-65, 91-92, 98); role matrix (69-73); version-based stale 409 naming who (77-80: 'Every card carries a version that changes whenever the card moves' rules out a from-stage/ABA alternative in protocol C); optimistic put-back with focus on that card (84-85); bulk board order 'by stage in the order listed above, then by place' (90-91); undo single-use, latest-only, note does not block, refused when touched or overfilling (96-100); activity lines newest first with job filter (110-113); live updates within 15 s preserving typing/focus/open card/conversation/scroll (117-123); Enter/Shift+Enter/blank refusal/failed send (138-140); paging and place-keeping (144-147); unread per person incl. 'sending counts as read' (151-160, matching the Mei Lin computation in functional U); seen rules incl. observer never counts and job's hiring manager counts (164-166); drafts per person/conversation/browser surviving reload and ended session with re-sign-in prompt (170-175; instruction.md:7 'or get signed out ... nobody else who signs in on that browser sees it'); note drafts per person per browser (rules.md:105-106, graded in hro_pol_session_resume); candidate wording and privacy list (179-194); status codes 401/403/404 (21-23). Every graded behaviour in tests/gates/* and tests/scored/*/judge.toml traces to one of these lines; I found no graded demand depending on an undisclosed default (routes, labels, layout and wording are explicitly free: rules.md:3-5, app_context.md:33-34). (5) Achievability is evidenced, not only argued: raw-evidence-index.json artifacts re-hashed MATCH and its matching_source_files equal the frozen solution bytes; results/workspace.json lists scripted golden groups all passed:true, run as uid 65534 with a real restart (stale move names who; bulk all-or-none and undo; candidate privacy; live board arrival_ms 810; drafts/Enter/Shift+Enter/seen/unread). This is scripted golden evidence only, not a configured judge run, Oracle or model score, which this row does not require. Ambiguities found (Notes, none blocking): N1 Workbook conflict: public 'Quality Checks' row 6 says network is allowed; 'Internal Quality Checks' row 6 says 'with no network'. Per SKILL.md Delivery profile ('Network is public in both phases') the public reading applies; under either reading nothing in this task needs network (CDN is optional), so no requirement becomes unreachable. Recorded, not silently resolved. N2 Status overlap for a candidate acting on someone else's card: rules.md:21-23 give both 'role does not reach an action -> 403' and 'application not theirs -> 404'. Both readings leak nothing. The golden returns 404 (solution/app/src/index.js:330); tests/scored/functional/judge.toml hro_refusal_status says 'refused with 403, or with 404 when the request names an application that is not theirs', which reads as accepting either; a strict judge reading could fail a role-first 403 app (weight 1, functional). Optional rewording suggested. N3 Unspecified but ungraded: whether hiring managers can view other jobs' boards/activity, whether a re-order or a rejection is itself an undoable move, multi-card reject/reopen, and whether cards displaced by another card's re-order count as changed. Protocols avoid relying on these (e.g. functional B(12) re-orders a different card Y one place, which does not displace A2), so no hidden requirement results. N4 Transport: rules.md:123 allows sockets for updates; an app sending commands (moves) over a socket instead of HTTP would leave replay-based role/anonymous/status rows without an observed HTTP request. The public rules frame refusals as HTTP 401/403/409, so the HTTP reading is the reasonable one; P3 latent. Counterexample attempts: no plausible broken app satisfies the instruction by a misreading (e.g. from-stage freshness instead of a version is excluded by rules.md:77). Conforming alternatives that could fail: only the N2 403-vs-404 wording edge (mitigated by the criterion's 'or') and the N4 socket-command edge; neither is a demonstrated failure.
suggested_fix: No fix required for this row. Optional hardening: in hro_refusal_status write 'refused with 403 or 404 (either is acceptable when the request names an application that is not theirs)'; optionally state in hireops_rules.md that actions are ordinary HTTP requests.
